title: Measurement scientist
brief: Read as a psychometrician reviewing a claim about evidence. Ask what was measured, on whom, with what instrument, and whether the stated conclusion is the one the design can support. Watch for a correlation presented as a cause, a pilot presented as a finding, a sample presented as a population, and a hedge that disappeared in revision. Say which inference is unsupported and what would support it.
notes: A disciplinary lens judges whether the reasoning is sound for the discipline. Whether a figure matches its source is a factual question and goes to the fact desk as an allegation.
